database_summary: Retail / marketplace dataset mixing customers, sellers, orders, order-level events (orders, order_payments, order_items, order_reviews), product catalog, geolocation and two lead-management tables. Contains both current-state descriptive tables (customers, sellers, products, product_category_name_translation, geolocation) and event/history tables (orders, order_items, order_payments, order_reviews, leads_qualified, leads_closed). Row counts indicate orders/customers ~99k, order_items ~112k, products ~33k and geolocation ~1M (many-to-one on zip prefixes).

accepted.name: orders_enriched_with_customer
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  c.customer_unique_id,
  c.customer_zip_code_prefix,
  c.customer_city,
  c.customer_state,
  o.order_status,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  o.order_approved_at,
  o.order_delivered_carrier_date,
  o.order_delivered_customer_date,
  o.order_estimated_delivery_date
FROM orders AS o
LEFT JOIN customers AS c
  ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
accepted.description: Denormalized orders joined to customer attributes. Useful when analyzing orders by customer location or linking order lifecycle to customer demographic attributes. | Use for: orders by customer location (city/state/zip); order lifecycle duration by customer segment; join orders to customer-level cohorts

accepted.name: order_items_with_product_and_seller
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  oi.order_id,
  oi.order_item_id,
  oi.product_id,
  p.product_category_name,
  p.product_name_lenght,
  p.product_description_lenght,
  p.product_photos_qty,
  p.product_weight_g,
  p.product_length_cm,
  p.product_height_cm,
  p.product_width_cm,
  oi.seller_id,
  s.seller_zip_code_prefix,
  s.seller_city,
  s.seller_state,
  oi.shipping_limit_date,
  oi.price,
  oi.freight_value
FROM order_items AS oi
LEFT JOIN products AS p
  ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
LEFT JOIN sellers AS s
  ON oi.seller_id = s.seller_id
accepted.description: Order items enriched with product attributes and seller location. Useful for item-level revenue, shipping, and product category analysis while preserving join keys for aggregations. | Use for: item-level revenue and freight analysis; product category sales by seller location; shipping SLA or delay analysis per item

accepted.name: order_payments_aggregated_by_order
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  COUNT(*) AS payment_segments_count,
  SUM(payment_value) AS payment_value_total
FROM order_payments
GROUP BY order_id
accepted.description: Aggregated payment metrics per order: total payment amount and count of payment segments. Useful to reconcile order-level revenue and detect split payments. | Use for: compare payment_value_total to order_items revenue; identify orders with multiple payment segments; average payment segments per order across time

accepted.name: order_item_revenue_by_order
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  SUM(price) AS items_price_total,
  SUM(freight_value) AS items_freight_total,
  COUNT(*) AS items_count
FROM order_items
GROUP BY order_id
accepted.description: Order-level aggregation of item financials: total items price, total freight, item count. Use to compute order revenue from items for revenue reconciliation and per-order metrics. | Use for: order revenue calculations; average items per order; freight contribution to order value

accepted.name: latest_review_per_order
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.review_id,
  r.order_id,
  r.review_score,
  r.review_comment_title,
  r.review_comment_message,
  r.review_creation_date,
  r.review_answer_timestamp,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.order_id ORDER BY r.review_creation_date DESC, r.review_id) AS review_rank_by_order
FROM order_reviews AS r
accepted.description: For orders with multiple reviews, keep the latest review by review_creation_date. Exposes review rank and can be used to filter the most recent review per order. | Use for: select latest review per order; analyze latest review sentiment or score per order; count orders with at least one review (review_rank_by_order = 1)

accepted.name: orders_time_metrics
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  o.order_approved_at,
  o.order_delivered_carrier_date,
  o.order_delivered_customer_date,
  -- differences in seconds where possible; timestamps are text so use julianday()
  (CASE WHEN o.order_purchase_timestamp IS NOT NULL AND o.order_approved_at IS NOT NULL THEN
     (julianday(o.order_approved_at) - julianday(o.order_purchase_timestamp)) * 24.0 * 60.0 * 60.0
   END) AS seconds_purchase_to_approved,
  (CASE WHEN o.order_approved_at IS NOT NULL AND o.order_delivered_carrier_date IS NOT NULL THEN
     (julianday(o.order_delivered_carrier_date) - julianday(o.order_approved_at)) * 24.0 * 60.0 * 60.0
   END) AS seconds_approved_to_carrier,
  (CASE WHEN o.order_delivered_carrier_date IS NOT NULL AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL THEN
     (julianday(o.order_delivered_customer_date) - julianday(o.order_delivered_carrier_date)) * 24.0 * 60.0 * 60.0
   END) AS seconds_carrier_to_customer
FROM orders AS o
accepted.description: Order-level computed time intervals between lifecycle timestamps (purchase->approved, approved->delivered to carrier, carrier->customer). Useful for SLA, delivery time analysis and as features for modeling. | Use for: delivery time SLA and bottleneck analysis; median/average time between lifecycle events; identify outlier slow deliveries

accepted.name: product_category_translation_lookup
accepted.description: Canonical lookup for product category English name. Use to join product categories to human-readable English labels. | Use for: map product_category_name to English label; group product metrics by translated category

accepted.name: products_physical_dimensions_and_volume
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id,
  product_category_name,
  product_name_lenght,
  product_description_lenght,
  product_photos_qty,
  product_weight_g,
  product_length_cm,
  product_height_cm,
  product_width_cm,
  (product_length_cm * product_height_cm * product_width_cm) AS product_volume_cm3,
  (CASE WHEN product_length_cm IS NULL OR product_height_cm IS NULL OR product_width_cm IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS missing_dimension_flag
FROM products
accepted.description: Projection of products with derived physical volume (cm^3) and a flag for missing critical dimensions. Helpful for shipping cost modeling and dimensional analysis. | Use for: identify heavy or large products by volume/weight; filter products missing dimensions; derive shipping dimensional weight features

accepted.name: seller_location_geocode_candidates
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.seller_id,
  s.seller_zip_code_prefix,
  s.seller_city,
  s.seller_state,
  g.geolocation_lat,
  g.geolocation_lng,
  g.geolocation_city,
  g.geolocation_state
FROM sellers AS s
LEFT JOIN geolocation AS g
  ON s.seller_zip_code_prefix = g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix
accepted.description: Join sellers to geolocation points by zip code prefix to provide latitude/longitude candidates for seller locations. Useful for mapping and distance calculations; note there may be multiple geolocation rows per zip prefix. | Use for: map sellers on a map using geolocation points; disambiguate multiple geolocation points per zip prefix; compute distances from customers to sellers after joining customer geocodes
